# Hermetic

> Hermetic is a local credential broker for AI agents on Linux. An agent asks
> for an API call by key name and URL; Hermetic decrypts the key inside its own
> processes, makes the authenticated HTTPS request and returns only the
> response. The key never enters the agent's process. Hermetic is in a private
> pre-release: public downloads return with v1.3.

## How it works

Keys live in an encrypted vault on the user's machine (Argon2id key derivation,
AES-256-GCM per key, HMAC-chained audit log). On the default path the agent
calls the MCP tool hermetic_authenticated_request with a key name and a URL.
Hermetic's daemon checks the key's rules and decrypts it; Hermetic's MCP bridge,
a separate process hardened for the length of the request, injects the key,
makes the call, wipes the key and returns the status, headers and body.
From a terminal, `hermetic request` does the same. For JWT signing (Pro) the
signing key never leaves the daemon and the agent receives a short-lived
access token.

Two other paths exist for tools that need them, and both are off by default:
handing a key to a program in its environment (`hermetic run`, the
hermetic_env_spawn tool, `hermetic proxy` for MCP servers), allowed per key;
and `hermetic reveal`, which prints one chosen key to a terminal.

## Key facts

- 5 credential types: static API keys, OAuth2 with refresh, AWS SigV4 and S3-compatible storage, JWT signing, SSH keys
- 170+ service templates; keys from 40 services are recognised by prefix
- New keys are brokered-only by default; `hermetic tier` allows one key to be handed to programs
- Per-key rules: domains, methods, paths, body size; 9 reference profiles; strict/advisory mode
- Destructive-endpoint floor: a built-in catalogue of irreversible endpoints across dozens of services, blocked by default, with optional ask-first approval
- `hermetic shield -- <agent>` runs an agent in Linux namespaces where the vault directory and Hermetic's processes are hidden (needs bubblewrap)
- Tamper-evident audit log with rollback detection; CLI only, no agent tool reads it
- Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Claude Desktop, VS Code, OpenClaw and any stdio MCP client
- Linux x86_64 only; single Rust binary; no telemetry; no network listener
- Open core: hermetic-core and hermetic-transport are AGPL-3.0-or-later; the daemon, CLI, bridge, proxy and dashboards are proprietary (free Community and paid Pro binaries)

## MCP tools

- hermetic_authenticated_request: brokered HTTP call; returns the API's response, never the key
- hermetic_list_secrets: key names and metadata, never values
- hermetic_env_spawn: run an allow-listed program with a key the user allowed to be handed to programs; returns the exit code
- hermetic_seal_vault: emergency lockdown
- hermetic_suggest_add: returns the command for the user to add a key (agents never handle key values)
- hermetic_sign_jwt (Pro): returns a short-lived access token

## Editions

- Community (free): the full security model, 10 keys, 1 environment, 7-day audit view (older entries kept), terminal dashboard
- Pro ($10/month at public release): unlimited keys and environments, OAuth2, SigV4 and S3-compatible storage, JWT signing, full audit history, web dashboard, usage and cost reports
- Enterprise: custom terms; contact dev@hermeticsys.com

## Known limitations

- A program already running as the user can make brokered calls while it runs; it cannot get a key through any agent-facing tool or change the vault without the passphrase. Keys the user allows to be handed to programs, and a reveal key if set, are readable by same-user programs.
- `hermetic start --remember-session` (opt-in) stores the passphrase in a form same-user programs can recover until reboot.
- No production deployments and no independent human security audit yet.
- Linux only. Containers need the IPC_LOCK capability.
